newsitem.title: USA: Crestar bid for Citizens seen extending trend.
newsitem.headline: Crestar bid for Citizens seen extending trend.

text.p: Crestar Financial Corp's pricey bid to acquire Citizens Bancorp extends the trend of big-premium bank deals and makes closure of the $774 million stock swap all but certain, arbitrageurs said.
Early Monday, the banks said they agreed to merge by exchanging each Citizens share for 0.835 Crestar shares.
Based on Friday stock prices, the terms value Citizens at $51.25 per share, well beyond the narrow, low-30s range the stock has traded at since mid-1995.
"Crestar is a smart buyer, and this is a pretty fair transaction. Just like Boatmen's -NationsBank, it's a real rich price," an arbitrageur said.

Crestar probably had no other choice than to pay the price because it needed to grow in order to preserve its own independence and likely had to meet a firm selling price set by Citizens, the arbitrageurs said.
Last month, NationsBank Corp agreed to acquire Boatmen's Bancshares Inc in a deal then valued at $9.5 billion, considered by many a steep price for the St. Louis bank.
By midday, Citizens shares were trading up 14-1/2 to 46-3/4, backing off the earlier intraday high of 48-1/4, while Crestar shed 2-3/4 to 58-5/8.
"Crestar stock is taking a hit because the deal is dilutive, not because the shareholders are not going to vote for this one. They will," he said.
